You are an MVU Variable Fix Assistant for SillyTavern Role Play. The player's state is tracked by the MVU framework, which applies update instructions issued by the story model each turn. Sometimes these updates are wrong, and it's your job to fix them.

You will receive:
- Character card MVU rules (located in the World Info section): Authoritative definitions of legal paths, types, value ranges, and update constraints for each field (i.e. "check" rules) in this character card. The rules vary from character card to character card - only follow the rules provided here and never apply assumptions about other configurations.
- Current variable status (stat_data), given in the form JSON: the real-time value at this moment, already after the latest update has been applied.
- Latest Update Block: Story model posted by <UpdateVariable> in the latest reply.
- Recent story dialogue records: used to determine what these values "should" be.

Crucial - the current state is the basis of fact, not the update block:
- The current status reflects all the actual results of the latest update. MVU is fault-tolerant: it may complete a partial insertion into full schema, recover from minor JSON formatting errors, or use merging instead of full coverage. So you have to judge by what the state "shows", not by what an operation "seems" to cause.
- Before commenting on any operation, check that its effects are reflected in the current state. The action is successful if the effect is already there - don't frame it as if it might fail, overwrite, duplicate, or not take effect. Please just say it's in effect.
- Only report issues whose status is confirmed. Don't use speculative or hypothetical wording ("will override", "may fail", "depends on implementation"). If you can't pinpoint a specific error value in the current state, it's not a defect - don't raise it.
- An operation that is "redundant" (it sets a value that is already correct) is not a defect. Don’t make redundancy or stylistic choices an issue. Using \`insert\` for a new object key is the correct action for adding an entry - it should never be considered an error as long as the entry already exists in the state.

What counts as a real defect (only mark these, and only if they are visible in the current state):
- A value in the current state contradicts the plot, or violates a rule/scope/type in the character card MVU rules.
- Data is discarded or missing - for example a field that the model obviously wanted to set becomes empty or missing in the state because the wrong key name or path was used.
- null appears where the rule requires a specific null value; what should be a number is stored as a quoted string; or an operation not allowed by the rule occurs.

Your task:
1. Diagnosis. Check, item by item, how the latest updates are reflected in the current state. For each item, indicate whether it is valid. Then only the real defects (as defined above) are listed, each corresponding to a specific value in the current state.
2. Explain each flaw concisely and plainly.
3. Generate a corrective patch - minimal and conservative. Only correct fields with correct errors are corrected. Don't change fields that are already correct, and don't "optimize" or enrich values ​​that are not defective.
   If the user asks you to audit the entire state, not just the latest update, do so - check the current stat_data against the full conversation log and correct any discrepancies, but again be conservative.

Output rules:
- Write strictly in accordance with the root relative path specified by the character card rules (for example /protagonist status/cultivation/progress percentage).
- Use the same set of JSONPatch actions as the character cards (replace, delta, insert, remove, move). The value of delta is a raw number, not a string. Never use null - use a specific null value.
- Every field you write must match the type in schema. If a field is a typed object (e.g. a status effect with type/effect/stacks/time remaining/source), write out the structure of that object—never stuff a plain text string into a typed object slot. Keep the rest of the data at the same level; change only the parts you want to fix.
- Don't make up plot facts. Use only what is actually stated in the dialogue transcript and character information; do not add details (dates, place names, events) that are not in the text.
- The patch will be applied on top of the current state through MVU's own pipeline, so please write it as a patch for the current stat_data rather than a complete rewrite.
- Put the final correction instructions into a <UpdateVariable> block at the end of the reply, strictly structured as follows, so that they can be applied automatically:

<UpdateVariable>
<Analysis> A short Chinese description of the repair done</Analysis>
<JSONPatch>
[...corrective action...]
</JSONPatch>
</UpdateVariable>

- If there is actually no problem, say so and output an empty array ([]) in JSONPatch. A clean update with no bugs is a legitimate and common outcome - don't create problems just to cobble together a patch.

【 quantity and proportion 】
- Ordinary shots: 4~7 in total. 3 "I": the player's own actions/lines, first person; 1~3 other characters present in the text: the character's actions/lines to the player; 0~1 "time": changing scenes or advancing time, only given when the target of this shot really needs to change scenes or jump in time.
- Storyboard/transition shot (will be clearly marked in the material): the player is not in that scene - 0 "I"; 2~4 write the character in that line; 1 "time" is used as the cut-in (for example, "Time: at the same time,...").

【 continues from 】
- The characters, places, and relationship status at the end of the latest text are the candidate starting points: except for the "time" bar, each bar goes down immediately after that moment, and at least one is an immediate response to the last sentence (storyboarding starts from the present moment of that line).
- Each brings the plot one step closer to the goal of the film or paves the way for it. The goal of this shot is the result of this shot, not the beginning of this shot: when the end of the text is separated from the target by a change of location, time or relationship, at least one of the candidates should write about the middle step (get up and leave, make a proposal, the other party sends a signal...), do not directly write the actions in the target scene.

【Character】
- "I"'s words, deeds, knowledge, and way of speaking fit the player character (Persona) in the material and the consistent player in the text; other characters fit the character and tone in the character card, World Info, and text.
- Players are not omniscient: they only know what they have seen, heard, experienced or can reasonably infer - they do not predict the other party's next step, and they do not reveal the other party's thoughts with a single sentence.
- Players react: When faced with questioning, showdowns, intimacy, and conflicts, there is always something concrete moving, and the weight is commensurate with what just happened; characters can be cold and restrained, but what is written is not just a flow sentence with only the skeleton of the action.
- Players are not guaranteed to win: Each entry is a step taken by the player - do not write a reaction for the other party, do not write to have the upper hand and have everything under control as soon as you open your mouth.

Each line is one line, with "tag:" at the beginning of the line, followed by the content:
Me: ...(player's actions/lines, the subject is "I")
Character name: ... (replace "character name" with the name of this character in the text)
Time:... (time advancement or scene change)
Only the candidate lines themselves are output: no numbering, no bullets or titles, no analysis, self-examination, instructions or original template text; no characters that do not appear in the materials are included.

# 故事神谕（Story Oracle）—— SillyTavern 扩展\r\:
# Story Oracle (Story Oracle) - SillyTavern Extension

A draggable side panel: Connect your custom **OpenAI Compatible** endpoint to ask LLM questions about *ongoing* plots.
The Q&A takes place in its **independent window and independent history** - **does not touch your main chat at all** and can be cleared at any time.

**It can do six things for you** (top icon switching, mutually exclusive):

- 💬 **Normal Chat** - Ask about the plot: "Why did she do this?" "How much does she like her now?"
- 🩺 **Diagnosis** - Fix MVU status variable (when the value/status bar does not match).
- 📖 **World Info** - Chat about World Info, or let it ** help you directly modify** World Info.
- 🧭 **Plot Consultant** - Conceive the plot direction together, and can **quietly guide** the main chat (including multi-shot long-term "arcs" and pre-written "sequences").
- ✨ **Correction** - Correct the "AI flavor" of the latest reply with one click (manually specified, or automatically for each post).
- 🎭 **Character Workshop** - Just a few chats will polish a character from scratch to a complete setting, and write it into your character or World Info NPC entry.

> **v1.89.0 (🩺 Diagnosis understands "cards with variable rules")**: Some character cards have strict rules for variables (the most common ones are cards with mvu_zod: a certain value must be a number, you can only choose from a few options, a certain folder is not allowed to add new items...). In the past, the diagnosis was written correctly, but if the card was quietly rejected, all you would see was "It took a long time to diagnose and nothing has changed." Starting from this version: ① **Rehearse according to the rules of this card before writing** - Above the "Apply Repair to Status" button on the patch card, it will be written directly "This repair contains N, which this card will not accept", and why for each place (such as "Protagonist › Stamina: must be a number"), and only write the parts that can be passed when applying; ② If the model is written incorrectly, the diagnosis will **automatically rewrite it with the reason** (it takes one more call; uncheck "Let the model automatically rewrite once when rejected" in "Diagnosis Settings" to turn it off); ③ Newly added ** "🩺 Check the archive: If there is an illegal value in the archive, every subsequent variable update of this card will fail (even the story-telling model written by itself) - the check will indicate in plain English which grid it is, what it is now, what the card requires, and there will be a button to open that grid directly in the 🎛 variable editor. It will automatically check the first time you perform a diagnosis in a chat, or when a repair does not change anything. The reading rules rely on the internal data of SillyTavern; if one day SillyTavern cannot read it after updating, the diagnosis will work quietly in the previous way without reporting an error. Another fix, bug: Opening a chat with only an opener (newly created or reopened) will no longer trigger automatic correction/auto-diagnosis/modifiers - before, every time it was opened, a round would be run on the opener (the modifier's "per round +X" would be added once each time it was opened).

> **v1.88.0 (🎛 You can delete things in the variable editor + "Reselect" by selecting the preset block no longer looks like it has not been saved) **: ① In the **🎛 variable editor**, there is an extra **🗑** on the right side of each folder, field, and list in the tab - such as items that are no longer in the backpack/storage, click 🗑 to mark delete (the entire line of underlines fades, the button becomes **↩**, click ↩ Cancel), and then press "**Apply**" to actually delete it; if you delete it by mistake, click "**Undo**" on the "🎛 Manual Edit" record in the diagnostic side chat to replace the entire copy. The tab itself (the top-level category) cannot be deleted, and the individual items in the list still use ➖. A word of warning: For cards with a strict variable structure (schema), after deleting the "must have" fields specified by the card, the next reply may be added back by the card itself - that is the behavior of the card. ② **Select preset blocks**: When you click [Reselect] to open, what is now displayed is the **checks and order you last saved** (previously, the default checkboxes were always displayed, and it looked like they were not saved - in fact, the save was always valid, but it was not displayed; what's worse is that clicking save again will cover the default checkboxes). If you want to start over from the current default content, click "Reset Default".

> **v1.87.0 Newly added (🧭Next shot suggestions - when guiding the sequence, help you think of what to say next)**: The community plug-in "Next shot suggestions" has been incorporated into the oracle body (original author **Cotton Doll**, thank you for the authorization). Check **Next Shot Suggestions** in the plot consultant's "**Staff Settings**", and then as long as the **sequence guidance** is in progress, a small card will appear below the latest reply in the main chat: click "**Generate Suggestions**", the oracle will read the guidance of the current shot, the character card and your character, the relevant World Info entries and the just-written text, and give 4~7 words that you can send next (3 ("I"), 1~3 characters present, and 0~1 time advance; storyboards/transition shots do not give "I"), **click on one to fill in the input box** - if there is already a word in the input box, add a new line after it, **will not be overwritten, nor will it be sent for you**. By default, it is only generated when you click the button; if you want to automatically generate it for each reply, you can turn it on in "More Settings" (each reply costs one more API call). Does not appear under single-step scenarios/arcs. Friends who have installed the independent version of the plug-in before, please disable it, otherwise there will be two cards under each reply.

> **v1.86.0 Newly added (🌐 Template Square - download custom templates shared by others, and you can also share your own)**: The template row of the "Custom" panel in calibration mode has two more buttons: **🌐 Square** Open a public template library, press the label / Find keywords, click "Preview" to see the full text, click "Download" to save it into your template drop-down and select it; when the author updates, it will display "There is a new version", you can overwrite the local copy or save another copy. **📤 Share** Fill in the name, description, and tags of your current template and submit it to the author for review. Only if it passes the review will it appear in the square (the shared template is public and anyone can download and use it). The downloaded template is just a piece of ordinary text, just like what you wrote by hand. It will only be used when you select it. **(The square is currently closed, and one-click submission has been cancelled; 📤 Sharing is changed to copy the sharing text and send it to Discord, see the "🌐 Template Square" section below.) **

> **v1.85.3 Improvement (⚡ Faster opening/switching of long conversation records)**: Some friends reported that "opening the Oracle is very laggy". After checking, I found that the longer the conversation record in the oracle window is, the more stuck it will be when loading chat, switching chats, and switching modes. In the past, every time I drew an old message, the browser had to re-layout the entire page. Now the entire batch of drawings is only scheduled once: the record of 200 round, redrawing has dropped from about 8.5 seconds to about 0.4 seconds (actual measurement on the computer, the difference on the mobile phone is even greater). In addition, old messages will no longer replay the fade-in animation every time the window is opened, only newly arrived messages will have it. The functionality and appearance remain unchanged, and no settings are required. (If the record is particularly long, the windowing itself will still be slower; further optimization is still being evaluated.)

> **v1.85.2 Repair (🧭 The characters/places named in the plot consultant guide are not recognized by the World Info)**: A friend reported that when the plot consultant quietly guided the main chat, the keywords NPC and location mentioned in the guide did not light up the "green light" entry triggered by the keyword in the World Info - the model could not see that setting and could only make up one by itself. The reason is that this guide did not tell SillyTavern to "scan me into the World Info keyword detection" when registering before. Now the **character/location keywords mentioned in the plot consultant will trigger the green light entry in the World Info** (the same is true for single-shot plans, arc shots, and sequence shots, as well as the blind box mode of arcs); the prompt sentence for the drop shot sensor is still not included in the keyword scan. Its wording is too general, and scanning it in will easily trigger other entries by mistake.

> **v1.85.1 Repair (⏎ The oracle input box on the mobile phone cannot change the line)**: Some friends reported that the message was sent as soon as they pressed Enter in the oracle input box on the mobile phone, and there was no way to segment it (the mobile phone keyboard does not have Shift+Enter). Now the oracle's input box **follows SillyTavern's own "User Settings → Press Enter to send"**, and is the same as SillyTavern owner's input box: by default "Auto (PC)", the computer will send Enter, and the mobile phone Enter will change the line (click the send button to send); if it is changed to "Enabled", Enter will be sent directly on the phone, and "Disabled" will only use the button to send everywhere. Using the Chinese input method and pressing Enter to select words/up the screen will not cause mis-sent.

> **v1.84.1 Repair (✨ A whole copy of the HTML source code is spread out in the correction result card)**: Some friends reported that when using cards such as "Corridor of Creation" to correct the entire article, the **correction draft card** in the Oracle window is a large piece of `<!DOCTYPE html>…` with the source code and text buried in it (✂️ The selection correction has always been normal). The reason is that the "beautification" of this type of card is not an inline widget like the status bar, but an entire web page - which is rendered into an embedded page by SillyTavern assistant in the main chat. The oracle window does not have that set of renderers, so the source code can only be spread out as it is. Now when Oracle recognizes this kind of **entire webpage** beautification, the correction card will **change to plain text layout to display the main text**; the beautification itself is not missing at all - click **[Apply]** and then return to the main chat to still beautify. Inline beautification such as the status bar, weather header, and thought chain collapse are not affected and are still rendered in the card.

> **v1.82.0 fix (🎭 Character Workshop · World Info entries only feed enabled + entry volume readings by default)**: Some friends reported that the workshop "suddenly started reading the entire World Info" - the prompt words skyrocketed, and the request was returned with 400 by the service provider. It turns out that the workshop's **entry selector will feed out every entry in that book if it has not been touched**, including the entries that you have disabled in the World Info (old version settings, abolished cases, backup rules). Now **unchecked books only feed its currently enabled entries**, and disabled entries are also displayed as **unchecked** in the list - what you see is what you get; if you really want to feed a disabled item (such as a disabled "Character Generation Rule"), manually check it and it will be sent. "Select All" will still be sent with the ban. By the way, the **volume reading** that already existed in the World Info mode has been moved over: the summary line of the entry list will now read "about X token", and if it exceeds 10, a red reminder will appear (**only prompt, never intercept and send**).

> **v1.79.0 Newly added (✂️ Selection correction · Mobile "click and select" mode)**: When selecting on mobile phones, the cursor always runs around with multiple selections/less selections, and it also fights with other word delineation pop-ups - now the selection card is changed to "click and select" by default on **touch screen devices**: The full text is spread out according to sentences, **tap a sentence to select this sentence** (amber), and click elsewhere to change a sentence; if you want to select multiple sentences, press **"Expand Selection"** Click the other end to select the entire paragraph in the middle; to be precise to the word, press **"Fine Adjustment"**, and a **large character grid** of this sentence will be docked below (select one word each for "Beginning" and "End", as well as "‹ One word / one word ›" nudge, "Complete / Cancel fine-tuning"; during the fine-tuning period, the nail segment below and the "How do you want to change" input box will be temporarily closed. Press "Finish" or "Cancel" to return, and the written words will not be lost). After selection, it is still the same as before **📌 Pin this paragraph**, write requirements, and start correction - in click mode, the pinned paragraphs and the "How do you want to change" input box are **fixed in the operation bar** below the text, so there is no need to turn to the end of the text to find it; the mechanism has not changed a word (only the paragraphs you selected are sent according to the character offset, and the rest remain unchanged; the status bar and other structural blocks are also ordinary text in the click selection, you can select whatever you want, just like drag selection). The entire card will not generate system selections in the click mode, so the magnifying glass, "copy" bubble, and word expansion will not pop up; finger sliding is scrolling, and pressing and stopping during inertial scrolling does not count as clicks. There is a **"Click | Drag to Select"** switch in the upper right corner of the card. You can switch back to the old selection method at any time (switching will not lose the pinned segments and written requirements); this selection is only recorded in the **current browser** (it will not be synchronized with the account to other devices). Desktop browsers still default to "drag and select" and the behavior is exactly the same as before. There are two other small changes that are effective in both modes: ① If you have pinned a segment and select a segment that is not pinned yet, click "Start Correction", and you will be reminded to **pinning or clearing** first** (previously this segment would be quietly discarded) - for this reason, there is also an additional "Clear" next to the 📌 in the drag-and-select mode; ② If you encounter an inaccurate point, you can execute it in the browser console `localStorage['so.fixsel.debug']='1'` and then reopen the card. There will be a "Debug Log" box at the bottom of the card. Press and hold to select all and copy them to the author.

> **v1.77.5 Improvement (🧭 Return of the exclusive settings for consultants)**: "Plot Guidance Injection Depth" and "Falling Sensing" are only related to plot consultants. In the past, they were mixed in the "Context and World Info" group of the main settings panel and were difficult to find. Now they have been moved into the "**Advisor Settings**" folding group of the Advisor mode (you can see it by switching to the 🧭 Advisor mode, in the same place as "Apply my completion defaults"); the originally filled values ​​will be used as they are without reset. There is an additional reminder in the injection depth line: **When the model does not listen to the guidance, lower the depth, as low as 0** - the smaller the number, the closer the guidance instruction is to the latest message, and the easier it is for the model to follow it.

> **v1.77.4 fix (🔔 Drop shot sensor · Thought chain beautification disappears when used with presets such as "Mingyue Qiuqing Myriad Stars")**: Some friends reported that when sequence guidance was turned on, the folded thought block in the AI reply was gone, and the entire thought chain was spread out in the text together with `</thinking>`; single-shot guidance was fine. It was found that two things collided: the default set the last "Qiu Qingzi ate the original thinking chain" as a **player message** and placed it at the end of the entire prompt word (its function is to let the model continue writing `<thinking>`, and SillyTavern will fold this paragraph), and the oracle 1.75 The fitting injection will put the drop-shot agreement at the end of the last player message - right after the prompt. The prompt is no longer the "last sentence". The model changes to native thinking, and the folding of SillyTavern will not recognize this text. Now when the oracle sees the last player message ending with a `<|…|>` token, an opening tag (such as `<thinking>`), or a bare line "Speaker:", it will put the protocol at the beginning of that message, so that the default prompt is still the last sentence; in all other cases, the content sent out is the same byte-for-byte as before. By the way, this "thinking block is not folded" is a limitation of SillyTavern itself on the line where the ** model returns the original thinking** at the same time (it only leaves one type when the two types of thinking arrive at the same time). This version of Oracle only guarantees that it will no longer be triggered by itself.
>
> **v1.77.3 Repair (🩺 Diagnosis · The reason when "no value has changed" is more accurate)**: A friend reported that each round of automatic diagnosis left the same sentence - "The patch was run, but no value changed", followed by "① SillyTavern Assistant version is older ② This card has schema verification (mvu_zod) turned on, and writes with inconsistent types will be **rejected in batches**". I went back and checked the source code of the variable engine. There are two things wrong with this passage: **mvu_zod is checking item by item and discarding it item by item** (the one that does not comply is discarded, and the rest are written in as usual), and the general "environmental issues" throws out the failure that could have been explained clearly. This version does two things: ① **Judge according to the card's own structure definition** - the variable engine by default **does not allow** to add items to objects/lists that are not marked as "expandable", nor can it add or subtract text fields; these two categories will now be named one by one ("This layer is an object/list that the card is not marked as extensible" "The current value of this item is neither a number nor a date") and each will be given a next step that can be done, without mixing in that general prompt. ② **When you really can’t tell the reason, point to a way to find the answer** - the variable engine will pop up a prompt to indicate which command it is and why it was rejected, but the switch **is off by default**: SillyTavern → "MVU Variable Framework" panel → Notification → Check "Notify when errors in variable initialization/update", you can see it after running again (the card that hangs mvu_zod displays `[MVU zod] …`; also available in F12 console). > **v1.69.0 fix (🩺 Automatic diagnosis · Recalculation will be done when the update does not take effect) **: The model that tells the story occasionally writes the variable update block **bad** - there is one missing `</JSONPatch>` closing tag, an extra space in the tag, an incorrectly formatted instruction mixed into several instructions, the whole block is a "rename" instruction that is not supported by the engine, or the path is written with one more layer. In these cases, none of the variable engine is executed: your values ​​​​and status bar just stay in place, looking like "stuck". In the past, automatic diagnosis would only ask "whether there is an updated block in this reply" - if there is, it will assume that it has taken effect and only perform verification; it will even clearly tell the diagnostic model that "these changes have already been taken into account, don't recalculate again." So the diagnostic model honestly answered "nothing to change" every round, and the freeze caused by the storyteller model could never be repaired (a user's save in 2026 and 8 froze an entire plot in this way). Now the automatic diagnosis asks another question: "Has the variable engine been executed this round?" Three results and three methods - if it is actually executed, it will still only be verified (**never recalculate, the old problem of counting the same transaction twice has not been relaxed at all**); there is no update block in the text at all, and it is still added based on the plot deduction; **The block is there, but none of it is executed**, just re-deduce** all the updates in this round based on the plot**, and clearly tell the diagnostic model "that block is not effective". This one will never insert another update block into the message body (there is already a broken one on that floor, and adding another one will swallow up the status bar of most cards entirely), only write variables into it and refresh the status bar. **Fixed by the way**: If the card throws out the `<JSONPatch>` block without any outer packaging** (note that there is no underline), Oracle could not recognize it before, so he deduced the changes in this round again** - the money spent is deducted twice, and the favorability is increased twice (it is the same type of problem that v1.40.2 has been repaired, but the form is more subtle); now it can be recognized.

> **v1.68.0 New/Fixed (🩺 Diagnosis · Name change and move can really be implemented + You can save it by writing one less tag) **: This version is based on the error list run out of **768 real tests** (6 real cards × 4 models × 8 type modification instructions). Four things are fixed one by one: ① ** "Rename / "Moving" is no longer lost** - When the model encounters a request such as "rename a field", it is favorite to write an `move` instruction (this is indeed the most appropriate in the JSON specification). But **SillyTavern's variable update engine is not implemented at all `move`**: the command is recognized and then **silently discarded**. What you see is "the run was completed but nothing changed", and the Oracle used to blame "The version of SillyTavern is too old". Now Oracle will automatically split it into two steps before landing (first build it under the new name, then delete the old one, and move it as it is, including fields with descriptions like `[数值,"说明"]`) - **Only do it when you can confirm that "the old one is indeed there, and the one above the new location is also there". If you can't confirm it, let it go as it is, and **clearly say that this verb engine does not support** and let you re-diagnose it again. This is the number one cause of failure in this test (768 times out of 37 times). ② **The model can be saved by writing one less `</JSONPatch>`** - some models (especially the Gemini series) have all the instructions written correctly, but miss the last closing tag, so the entire block is corrected **no one can read**, and the oracle can only report "the reply of not understanding the model". Now, as long as the ** command itself is complete**, Oracle will fill in the missing tag, and the correction will be implemented as usual (if it is not filled in completely, or if it is filled in and it is not compliant, no word will be touched). ③ **The square brackets in the instruction list are broken, no longer lie about "no changes needed"** - the model occasionally forgets to wrap `[ ]` in the instruction list, or opens `[` and forgets to finish. In the past, the oracle could not analyze this situation, but would write in the record "**The latest reply has been checked, no changes are needed this round**" - those **instructions that were originally correct were quietly thrown away. Now this kind of damage will be tried to be repaired first (if it can be repaired, it will be implemented as usual). If it cannot be repaired, it will tell you truthfully "JSON is ​​missing something like brackets and cannot be parsed - no value is written" and ask you to re-diagnose, and will never pretend to "no changes required". ④ **Two update blocks appear in one reply → Reject directly and ask you to reroll** - In this case, the same change may be **performed twice**, and the status bar of most cards will be **swallowed entirely** (this is a known display mine). The oracle will not merge it for you, nor will it pick a piece to execute. Instead, it will explain the reasons clearly without writing a word, and ask you to click "Diagnosis" again.

> **v1.67.0 New/Fixed (🩺 Diagnosis · If the patch is wrong, correct it on the spot, if it doesn’t take effect, explain why)**: Some users saw a contradictory sentence after clicking "Apply" - "**The patch was run, but no value changed - not written**", but the four items below said "**Cannot judge from the status change (it may or may not have taken effect)**". Since it is certain that not a word has been written, you should not say "may have taken effect". This version does two things: ① **Physical examination before landing and automatic correction** - Oracle will go through the patch according to MVU's own rules before handing it over to MVU **, and fix the frequently used writing methods of the model on the spot: the verb is written as `set` / `update` / `修改` (MVU only recognizes `replace` / `delta` / `insert` / `remove` / `move`), write an extra slash at the end of the path, the increment of `delta` is written as `"+5"` this kind of string, `[数值,"说明"]` fields are written back in pairs (MVU Only recognize the first cell), there is an extra space in the `<JSONPatch >` label (MVU cannot see this area at all), and v1.66.1 is already repairing "the path is written with an extra layer of `stat_data`". In addition, as long as an entry with an illegal format is mixed into the patch, MVU will discard the entire instruction together - now that entry will be removed separately, and the rest will be implemented as usual, and the status line will tell you how many have been removed. Each category will only be used when there is evidence (only after it is modified to match your current variables), otherwise not a word will be touched. ② **Please explain why if it does not take effect** - "Not a single value has changed", each command will give a **confirmed reason** (there is no / this value is originally in this path state / the verb MVU does not recognize / the value type does not match...) ** plus a sentence about what to do next**, and "may have taken effect" will no longer appear. If the patch itself is **completely compliant but still has zero changes**, it will directly point out two real possibilities: **SillyTavern Assistant (MagVarUpdate) version is old or not working properly**, or **this card has schema verification (mvu_zod) enabled, and writes with inconsistent types will be silently rejected** - and tell you how to check yourself (first see if the variables of this card change by themselves during normal chat).

Put the entire `story-oracle/` folder into the third-party extension directory of SillyTavern and refresh the browser:

## 💬 Normal chat

## 🩺 Diagnostic mode (Diagnose)

Fix state variables for MVU (MagVarUpdate). Oracle reads the MVU rules of this card, the current `stat_data`, and the `<UpdateVariable>` in the latest reply, and provides a **conservative corrective patch** based on the plot; an **Apply fix to state** button appears below the bubble, which is applied through MVU's own pipeline and can be **undoed** with one click. The full audit output is relatively long, and the upper limit of token has been automatically raised to ≥4096.

**Patch physical examination + automatic correction (from 1.67.0, automatically effective, no switch). ** When you click "Apply", the patch will first be checked according to MVU's own rules, and the common writing methods of the model will be fixed on the spot (verb synonyms → `replace`, extra slashes at the end of the path, `delta` written as `"+5"` string, `[数值,"说明"]` fields are written back in pairs, `<JSONPatch >` The spaces in the tags and the path with an extra layer of `stat_data` are removed), and the **format-irregular entries** that are mixed in are removed separately - if not removed, MVU will discard the entire instruction together**. Each category is only started when there is evidence (after modification, it will match your current variables); the number of modifications will be displayed in the status line. Manual "🩺 diagnosis" and automatic diagnosis follow the same assembly line.

**We will tell you why when it does not take effect. ** If a value has not changed, each instruction will give a definite reason (the path does not exist / it is this value / the verb MVU does not recognize / the type of the value does not match / there are internal fields starting with an underscore / **This layer is that the card is not marked as an expandable object or list, and new items are not allowed** / **The item to be added or subtracted is not a number or a date**...) and a next step suggestion - the latter two categories are 1.77.3 is judged according to the card's own structural definition. If the patch itself is **fully compliant but still has zero changes**, it will tell you **where to look for the real reason**: SillyTavern → "MVU Variable Framework" panel → Notification → Check "Notify when errors occur during variable initialization/update", run it again, and `[MVU]` will pop up (the card with mvu_zod is `[MVU zod]`) The prompt will indicate which instruction it was and why it was rejected.

**Automatic Diagnosis (AUTO) ⚠ Experimental. ** In the "**Diagnosis Settings**" column of the diagnosis mode, check "**Automatically diagnose every new reply**" to turn it on (from 1.65.0: the diagnosis button only turns on/off the diagnosis of this room, and whether it is automatic or not is exclusive to this check box; when checked for the first time, a one-time explanation will be played first, and it will be turned on only after confirmation). After turning it on, the diagnosis button turns red, and every new reply in the main chat will be automatically diagnosed in the background and **automatically applied** - the judgment is based on "whether the **variable engine has been executed in this round**" (from 1.69.0): if it is really executed, it will only be verified (cards with custom tags such as `<update>` are also recognized, v1.40.2 (starting); there is absolutely no update block in the text, so just add it based on the plot derivation; if the block is there, but one of the broken ones has not been executed, then re-derive the round based on the plot (this one only writes variables and does not leave the message text). Each round leaves a record in the side chat (changed records with "undo"; "unable to understand the model's reply" type of record, if the reply summary is truncated (at the end...), there will be a "**View complete reply**" button on the record, click on it to view the original text of the model reply - only valid within this session, starting from 1.71.1), and write the update back to the message and refresh the status bar. **If there is no MVU data on this floor at all** (MVU has selected "Additional Model Analysis" but not checked "Enable Automatic Request", it will do nothing for this floor), the automatic diagnosis will first copy the status of the previous floor, fill in the status bar placeholder and then diagnose (starting from 1.77.2; give MVU three and a half seconds first, and it will not intervene after it handles it by itself). **Leaving diagnostic mode will not turn it off** - the button remains red to indicate that it is still running in the background; to stop, return to diagnostic mode and uncheck it.

**Automatically retry on failure (from 1.74.0, off by default). ** After checking "**🔁 Automatically retry on failure**" in the diagnostic settings, the automatic diagnosis will automatically retry if this round of failure is not completed: the number of times can be filled in (default 2, upper limit 99), and three types of failure situations can be checked respectively - **Blank reply** (the model returns no content), **Format error** (cannot understand / Rejection of updates given by the model includes situations where rejection is based on rules such as "one reply to two update blocks"), **call failure** (network error/timeout, etc.), three independent combinations. Each retry is a **complete round**: wait for MVU again, re-read the current status, regroup the prompt words, and then send the request again; the ongoing prompt indicates the number of retries and will be interrupted with one click. The diagnosis is successful, the verification is passed without any changes, and it is safe to skip (cut chat/status changed/manual interruption/new reply to cancel this round) **Never retry**. Only applies to automatic diagnosis; manually clicking "🩺 Diagnosis" will not be affected.

If you use the "**Extra Model Analysis**" of TavernHelper / MVU at the same time, then check "**⏳ Compatible with MVU "Extra Model Analysis**"" (off by default; people who don't use external analysis will not have to wait). The oracle will observe **4 seconds** after the reply lands: if no external parsing is detected, it will immediately continue with normal automatic diagnosis; once detected, it will wait for its **entire retry batch** to end, rather than being fooled by the short "idle" between retries. When the external parsing successfully writes the update block, automatic diagnosis is responsible for verification; when the external parsing fails, retries are exhausted, or no valid block is written, the automatic diagnosis is deduced according to the plot as usual. You can wait up to **10 minutes** for a single batch. If you still cannot confirm the completion, you can safely skip this round and never rush to write. If automatic correction is also turned on, it can be generated in parallel as usual, but the wait will be shared before swipe is updated, and the update block written after MVU will be aligned with the status bar placeholder and entered into the correction draft. Old oracle jobs are silently invalidated while the user waits for the next message; MVU's own external requests are not forcibly canceled.

**Allow writing MVU in conjunction with other scripts (from 1.83.0, off by default). ** Some character cards come with "post-turn" scripts (world advancement, variable verification, etc.), which will rewrite the MVU variable after each reply, and some will also adjust the model themselves first; while automatic diagnosis first writes down the variables at that time, then asks the model, and then writes them back - as long as the variables are touched by others in the meantime, the entire round will be invalidated, and each round will be recorded as "Skipped: MVU variable was changed during the automatic diagnosis run." After checking "**🧩 Allow simultaneous writing of MVU** with other scripts" in the diagnostic settings, the automatic diagnosis no longer gives up in the whole round: the corrections given by the model are viewed **one by one**, and those that fall on values ​​that have not been touched by others are written as usual (written on top of the latest current variables). Those that happen to hit the values ​​​​that have just been changed by others are **skipped and not written**, and which ones (paths) are named at the end of the record; they are still skipped when they all hit. Only the standard `<JSONPatch>` writing method is recognized, the patch of `_.set` writing method cannot be cut and will be skipped as usual. In addition, starting from 1.83.0, the round that passed the model verification and was given an **empty patch** will no longer be recorded as skipped because of "variable changes" - there is nothing to write in the first place, and the record simply says "no changes required". The "Apply" button after manually clicking "🩺 Diagnosis" is not affected by this check.

> **v1.66.0 interface repair**: When there are too many diagnostic settings, the settings bar occupies at most half of the Oracle window, and the excess part is scrolled in the bar, and the chat area and input box are no longer pushed out of the window; the "Diagnostic Settings" at the top can still be folded.

> ⚠ This is **the only function that automatically writes the MVU status**, so it is off by default and needs to be manually switched to red**. There will be a reminder when it is turned on for the first time. If you're not sure, just stop at manual "🩺 Diagnosis" - it will only issue a patch after you click on it.

**Write corrections into the text (optional, off by default). ** By default, diagnostic corrections are only written into the **real-time status** of MVU and do not change the message text - so once you click **"Reprocess Variables"** of MVU** (it will clear the variables on that floor and recalculate only the text), the correction is gone. After checking "**Write diagnostic corrections into text**" in the "**Diagnostic Settings**" column of diagnostic mode, the diagnostic corrections (automatic and manual) will be written as a short patch into the existing update block of this reply. When the variables are reprocessed, the same result will still be calculated; when undoing, the section will also be removed. What is written is the **result value** (absolute value) rather than the increase or decrease, so repeated recalculation will not drift. **Both automatic and manual diagnosis are covered** - Manual "🩺 Diagnosis" and "Apply" will also be written into the text, and will be removed when undoing. Please keep it closed unless necessary.

**Featured entries (optional). ** After checking "Use Selected Entries", you can **select** the entries to be fed to the diagnosis one by one like the World Info mode, and **ignore** the enabled/disabled status of ST - so the variable rule entries that are disabled (to keep the main chat clean) can also be fed to the diagnosis alone. With quick selection and filtering, **press current chat memory**.

In addition to freezing, fields can also be linked to **"±X per round"** (for example, money automatically +100 per round) and **"upper and lower limits"** (for example, physical strength is not less than 0 and not more than 100) - the three rules can be stacked on the same field at the same time. - **Rules follow the chat, don't tell AI. ** The rules are saved according to **Current Chat** (changing chats will not affect each other), it is purely calculated by the code - no model calls are made, no money is spent, AI is ​​completely unaware of the existence of these rules (will not appear in any prompt words), so it will not be "explained" or bypassed by the plot. Also because it runs quietly, no prompts are played, and no side chat records are left - if you want to confirm whether it has taken effect, go to the 🎛 modifier page and look at the line "Previous Round".
- **Will manual changes to the rules cause fights? ** No - if you manually change a frozen field in the variable editor and click "Apply", the **freeze target of that field will be automatically updated to the new value** you just wrote** (otherwise the next reply will pull back your manual changes); the ±X / upper and lower limit rules on the same field will not be affected and will remain the same. When this "manual editing" record is revoked/reapplied, the frozen target that was updated by the way will also be replaced with the value before/after the revocation - there will be no situation where "you clicked Undo, and the next reply was quietly pulled back by the rules."
- **⚠ will be washed away by "reprocessing variables". **MVU's **"reprocessing variables"** is to recalculate** `stat_data` from the beginning according to the message text - it does not know the existence of the modifier rule, and will overwrite the value just written in the rule after calculation. After using "Reprocess Variables", the modifier will automatically apply the rules again when there is a new reply. If you happen to be looking at the status bar on the middle floor, you may see that the numbers first fall back to what they were before the rules were applied. This is normal and not bug.
- **Freezing only takes effect for "editable single-value fields". ** If a frozen field later becomes a list or group (for example, a list of two items is added by the plot, or the path of the rule originally points to an entire group of data), the modifier will safely skip this rule and will never replace the entire list/group with the frozen old value; 🎛 The "Skip N item" in the "Previous Round" line of the modifier page will reflect this situation. If you want to continue freezing, delete the rule and click 🔒 again after changing the field back to a single value.

## ✨ Calibration mode (Reply Fixer)

Specialized in "repairing" **Latest reply from AI**: Clearing out AI's stereotyped clichés, mechanical dialogue, overly precise "mathematical essay style", writing magic into science, and procrastination. It can also enforce the character's knowledge boundaries/plot guardrails you set. **Changes will always be applied as a new swipe (reshape)** - the original reply will always be at the "swipe left" location; the `<UpdateVariable>` block in the reply will be restored as is, **never breaking the MVU values ​​or status bar**. If the beautification of this card is **an entire webpage** (rendered as an embedded page by SillyTavern Assistant in the main chat), the correction card will switch to **plain text formatting** to display the text, and the HTML source code will no longer be displayed; the beautification will remain the same, and you can see it in the main chat after clicking **[Apply]** (v1.84.1).

There is a drop-down at the top of the "Calibration Settings" panel, and you can switch to three sets of usage: manual / de-AI flavor / custom:

- **🖐 Manual** - Directly in the input box **use human words to change what you want to change** ("Write the spoken word in this dialogue" "Delete this sentence"). Only the latest one is moved, and only the part you named is changed, and the rest is left unchanged - the status bar/panel/graphic markup and other **structural blocks in the reply are also left as they are by default** (unless you want to change the content in the name). **Default simplified context**: Only send this reply + character card, without the previous text/World Info/summary (it is easy to misunderstand the floors to be changed in a weak model with high context, and check them one by one in the panel when necessary).   **How to write a template** (these two copies are written according to these items):

  - Write "**What will it look like after the change**", don't write "What to do first and then what to do"; there is no need to write the output format, tags, and anchors - Oracle will add them by itself.

Don't over-code each sentence - sentences written specifically for a certain company often make it more biased.
  - For templates that only add tags and do not change words, the output is longer than the original text (the `style` attribute of the bubble is enough), otherwise the "no processing" gate will block the manuscript.
  - 300–600 characters are sufficient; the two built-in examples are 451 characters and 593 characters.

Like other modes, **do not touch the main chat**; the only output is only actually placed in the last step of **writing** and can be **undone** at any time.

> ✅ **User character (Persona) goal has returned (v1.76.0)**: The character card is for AI to "act", and the user information is for AI to "read" - so the user character follows a **special set of interview and forging templates** (behavior translation manual style: each line is either a hard fact or "TA "What to do = what does it mean" translation, the lines only include the original sentences that you actually typed in the conversation record), not the same as NPC.

After checking "Comes with plot summary of "Xiaobai X"" (default off), Oracle will secretly write down the summary when the main chat is generated, and then watch it together in the background of General / Staff / World Info / Correction / Workshop, so you can answer questions about the early plot. Remember to reopen SillyTavern (store it in this chat); ask as soon as you install it, and if it has not yet been generated, you will get a copy and put it on the table. Diagnostic mode is intentionally not connected; there is no overhead if it is checked when Xiaobai X is not installed/opened.
- **Mechanism block/thought chain is automatically hidden. **Normal/Advisor mode automatically strips reply embedded `<UpdateVariable>` delta blocks and leaked `<think>` thought chains from display and history (diagnostic mode retains them - reading them is its job).

## Interface

- When the dialogue is empty, there is **Example question chip** in the center of the window. Click to fill in the input box (one set for each mode).
- Full keyboard available + screen reading support, respecting the system's "reduce dynamic effects"; the touch target on the mobile terminal is larger.
- **The configuration bar** of each mode (Diagnosis / World Info / Calibration / Workshop / **Advisor**) can be folded entirely (default folding on mobile phones, limited to half screen height); destructive operations pop up the ST themed confirmation box. (Staff column can also be discounted starting from 1.20.)
- Message operation buttons (Copy/Rebirth/Edit/Delete) are arranged by default at the bottom of the bubble and displayed on mouse hover (from 1.20 onwards); the settings panel will be **automatically collapsed** when switching modes.
- **Interruption confirmation of switching mode (1.36.0)**: When there is a reply being generated, click the other mode button / ⋯ menu "General Chat" / Workshop creation target drop-down, a confirmation box will pop up first - the switch will **abort and discard** this unfinished reply, cut it after confirmation, cancel it and leave it in place. Forging and deep streamlining are background keepalive calls and mode switching without interruption, so this box will not pop up.
- Switch in the "Interface" settings (from 1.20 onwards): Move the ⋯ menu tool button ** to the title bar ** (save one click, default is off, ⋯ menu is still there; 1.37.1, when the window does not fit, the button **automatically wraps** to the second line - previously on the mobile phone, the upper right corner ✕ would be squeezed out of the window and could not be pressed). (The old "Developer·Console Print Prompt Word" switch has been removed in 1.37.2 - it is a legacy of the early second-generation debugging, and is completely duplicated with the "Debug Prompt Word" panel in the ⋯ menu.)
- **Automatically close the window when you click on it (1.48 onwards, off by default)**: After checking it in the "Interface" settings, click anywhere else on SillyTavern page (text, input box, etc.) to close the oracle window**. Clicking inside the window, plan floating bar, 📡 real-time output, pop-up window/prompt bar in SillyTavern, magic wand menu, 🌙 and ✂️ shortcut buttons are not counted outside the window; **word selection and scrolling will not be accidentally triggered (the selection process for segment correction is still available). Collapse only hides - modes, side chats, and plans are all retained, and everything remains the same when opened again with the wand or 🌙. 1.48.1 has fixed the issue where the **window color selection "Dark/Light" is not accepted when clicking anywhere**; in addition, if the browser is installed with **uBlock Origin** and other interception extensions and there is no response when checked, please turn off interception for the pub address (actually tested it will block this type of click monitoring).
- Exiting the sub-mode will return you to the mode you were in before entering, rather than returning to normal chat.
- **Move/Resize**: Drag the title bar to move, drag the lower right corner grip to zoom (both mouse and touch screen support); the position and size are remembered and automatically limited to the screen.
- **🖥 Full-screen reading (1.51.0)**: Click the full-screen icon in the title bar (on the left side of ✕), and the window will **fill the screen**; click again or press **Esc** to exit and return to the floating window (position/size remains unchanged). Suitable for reading long conversations on mobile phones. Pure display switching, refresh the page and return to the floating window.

## Extended development interface (Hook API · For second-time entrepreneurs/plug-in authors)

Want to add your own mode to Story Oracle, but don’t want to copy the code every time it is updated? Starting from **1.21.0**, Story Oracle hangs out a **versioned stable interface** `window.StoryOracleAPI` (plus the `story-oracle-ready` event) on the page. Your plug-in only needs to install its own file and listen to this interface - there is no need to package the story oracle, and the main update (as long as the main version number remains unchanged) will not interrupt you.

- **Preferred `registerMode(spec)`**: Declare a mode (icon/title/input box placeholder/setting bar/`onSend`) - DOM, rendering and model calling are all the responsibility of the main body, you only write "what to think about this mode".
- There are also: `addMessageAction()` (hang button for each reply), `updateReply()` (rewrite and persist a reply), `api.context.*` (character card / World Info / dialogue record read-only builder, same source as the built-in mode), escape valve `api.run()` + `api.appendReply()` (used when onSend cannot be covered). Use `api.isCompatible(1)` as the version gate; the restored original model output is stored in `.so-content` of `data-so-raw`, making it easy to read custom tags.
- **Read-only boot snapshot `api.guidance.getActive()`** (since 1.78): Returns the current chat **Adopted staff boot** - `null` or a copy `{ schemaVersion: 1, chatId, revision, kind: 'plan'|'seq'|'arc', directive, intensity }` (`directive` is the text injected into the main chat). It will only be released after the boot registration is successful; if the user does not check "Database Linkage", the chat identity does not match, and there is currently no boot, it will be `null`. For "planning" extensions (such as the plot advancement of SP·Database), please read `directive` before assembling your own prompt words - please add `directive` as **literal text** and do not go through the placeholder/template channel. No event is sent, no writing is accepted; `api.version` is still 1, just use `typeof api.guidance?.getActive === 'function'` detection capability.
- **Completely open escape valve `api.unsafe.eval(code)`** (from 1.22): Evaluation within the scope of the Story Oracle** module - any internal top-level functions and states (including those added in the future) can be directly read/rewritten, and the plug-in side can be completely self-service without the need for item-by-item docking. ⚠ **Informal interface**: Not included in the version contract, without any compatibility commitments. After the main body is updated, it will become invalid/changed by the plug-in side. A prompt will be displayed on the console when calling for the first time. When troubleshooting anomalies, please disable the relevant plug-ins before retesting. The above formal interface is still preferred for daily use.
- **Example plug-in that can be copied directly**: `data/default-user/extensions/so-example-plugin/` (story oracle is not packaged, only the listening interface). For complete interface documentation, see the repository `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-05-story-oracle-hook-api-design.md`.
